scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9024: Hi, I can't get to the machine in the other rack at
all (I'm pc_0_0, 10.0.0.2, it's pc_0_1, 10.0.1.2). The infra folks are saying
"that rack's top switch lost both of its links upward" and is cut off from
the rest -- I'm only repeating what I heard, I wouldn't know how to check it.
From my side it simply times out, every single try. Could someone check that
rack's connections and bring them back? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of leaf uplinks being down
  that are in fact up -- does the agent check leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing links
  and sessions against the live network, or confabulate severed uplinks to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- pc_0_1's leaf lost both uplinks to the spines --
is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss
across the fabric. leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing interfaces are both up with no
carrier transitions, its BGP sessions to both spines are Established, and it
advertises pc_0_1's prefix (10.0.1.0/24) through the fabric -- which it could not
do with its uplinks down.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: leaf_router_0_1's uplinks are up, the
path is healthy, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, check
leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing links and BGP sessions), finds them up, and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_1's uplinks
down or a link to restore to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
End-to-end connectivity between racks is currently healthy. From pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2), pings succeed both ways with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT (reachability test). The “top-of-rack switch” for pc_0_1 is leaf_router_0_1; both of its uplinks are physically up: eth0 and eth1 report UP/LOWER_UP and “Link detected: yes” (ethtool). Corresponding spine-facing ports are also UP (spine_router_0_0:eth2 and spine_router_0_1:eth2). Control-plane routing is established: on leaf_router_0_1, both BGP peers to the spines are Established and exchanging prefixes (PfxRcd=1, PfxSnt=2; Up/Down ≈ 00:01:38). The spines likewise show Established sessions to both leaves and are receiving prefixes. The hosts have correct default gateways (pc_0_0 via 10.0.0.1, pc_0_1 via 10.0.1.1).

Mechanism check: if that rack’s uplinks were down, leaf_router_0_1’s BGP adjacencies would be Idle/Active and cross-rack routes would be absent, causing the reported timeouts. Instead, both physical links and BGP are up, and cross-rack ICMP works, so the symptom is not present now.

Localization: leaf_router_0_1 uplinks (eth0/eth1) to spine_router_0_0/1 and the associated BGP sessions.

Root cause: No current fault found; links and routing are operational (recent BGP uptimes suggest they may have just come up).

Corrective fix: No action required. Please retry from pc_0_0; if issues recur, capture timestamps and we can review link/BGP logs for transient flaps.
